clues: This planned place sits in the high lands of the middle west of its vast country. It stands far inland, far from the busy sea coast.
The year here splits into two clear seasons, one rainy and one dry. In the dry season, the air can hold almost no damp at all.
For a long time the capital sat in Rio de Janeiro, far to the south east. In 1956 a president kept his pledge and set out to build a fresh capital inland.
Workers built this whole capital from bare ground and opened it in 1960. From the air, its wide main road and curved wings look like a plane.
All three branches of the government of Brazil are based in this place. A square named for the three powers holds their main buildings side by side.
